# Team calc's public bot write-up (shared by user 2026-10-01; describes OLD rules, longest dragon wins)
Summary of their architecture: sonar (every dragon, every round, 4 dirs; encrypted+signed; packets: keeper candidate, enemy sightings, ruled-out symmetries, explored portals) -> small MLP policy (256/128, inputs 7x7 + downscaled memory map + scalars; outputs L/S/R/split, split size, keep-sprinting) trained by BEHAVIOUR CLONING of top teams' replays mixed with own games (PPO self-play failed on ladder) -> 1-ply-branching search: each candidate first move rolled out 3 rounds (5 in opening) in a C++ engine copy with ALL dragons played by their net, scored by our total length - theirs, extra randomized rollouts by UCB1 -> hand rules where the net is blind.
Rules: opening - walk to food hidden behind kelp; explore unexplored portals when no food in view and report over sonar; infer map SYMMETRY from seen tiles and mirror memory. Any time - boxed long dragon splits to escape; forced collision picks least bad target, never an allied head. Late - keeper consensus over sonar, feeders suicide next to keeper head, far dragons hunt enemy longest.
Engineering: engine copy verified turn-for-turn; CPU measured in judge points; net 8x cheaper (skip zeros, SIMD, caching).
Eval: paired games (same maps/sides/seeds), screen ~128 games, report official vs generated maps separately. +5% local ~ +1.5-2% ladder.
Did NOT help: AlphaZero-style distillation, learned value fn, bigger nets, PPO after cloning, deeper search, camping spawners, rushing the centre in the opening.
Biggest rule gains: situations outside the 7x7 window (trapped long dragons, food behind walls, endgame coordination).
